title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning — queueing fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Alyssa Chen
description: Motivation: production traces showed the continuous batcher scheduler could cause starvation of short/low-token requests when long sequences dominated the queue, and occasional head-of-line blocking due to strict FIFO semantics. This PR introduces a set of scheduler tunings to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation, and bound waiting time via timeouts. Changes include: (1) age-aware priority: requests accrue priority as they wait, preventing indefinite starvation of short requests; (2) weighted queue admission: small-token requests receive a higher admission weight to reduce tail latency for interactive traffic; (3) preemptive dispatch window: allow a bounded preemption of large batches when high-priority requests exceed a threshold; (4) per-request max-queue-time timeout and graceful fallback: if a request exceeds its configured queue timeout, it either falls back to a lower-cost model variant or returns an explicit timeout error (configurable per-route); (5) KV-cache warmup hints: when small requests are admitted into a batch with a long-sequence request, we move hot prefix KV entries earlier in the execution order to reduce cache thrashing; (6) new metrics and tracing hooks for queue wait time, preemption events, and per-priority latency. The description below contains a short checklist and results summary. Checklist: - [x] Implement age-based priority and admission weights - [x] Add preemption window and configurable thresholds - [x] Add per-request queue timeout with route-level config and default 200ms - [x] Update KV-cache warmup ordering heuristics - [x] Add unit and integration tests covering fairness and timeout fallbacks - [x] Add perf canary and dashboards for new metrics - [x] Update runtime docs and release notes Relevant Linear tickets: ENG-3421, ENG-3498. Backwards compatibility: all defaults preserve previous behavior (FIFO semantics) unless the deployment toggles the new scheduler flags; timeouts are off by default in older configs. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated; gradual rollout on Dedicated clusters starting with canary pool, monitor q_wait_time and p99_latency and enable preemption only if p99 improves without throughput regressions.

diff_summary: Key code changes: - scheduler.py: refactored dispatch loop to account for per-request priority and age; added bounded preemption window and admission sanitizer. (~+260 lines) - policies.py: new AdmissionPolicy and AgingPriorityPolicy encapsulate weight and age calculations with tunable parameters. (~+120 lines) - kv_cache/warmup.py: added ordering hint API to move hot prefixes earlier in execution when mixed-token batches detected. (~+90 lines) - queue_metrics.py: new counters and histograms (queue_wait_ms, preempt_count, priority_level_latency_pXX). Tests and docs added.
review_conversation: Priya: Can we land this without the preemption window turned on by default? Preemption increases scheduling complexity and could harm throughput. Alyssa: Agreed, preemption is feature-flagged and off by default; default is age-priority only. Omar: Please add a unit test that simulates continuous long sequences to prove short requests don't stall. (added test_scheduler_fairness.py). Sam: The per-request timeout default of 200ms seems optimistic for high-load regions; can we make it route-configurable and documented? Alyssa: Timeout moved to route config with a safe default and docs updated. Priya: LGTm after small nits on naming and a logging improvement. Omar: Approve after tests pass. CI initially failed integration (flaky test), rerun fixed it. Merged via squash on 2024-11-15.
ci_summary: CI run breakdown: lint: pass; unit: pass; integration: failed on first run due to timing-sensitive test (fixed by increasing test tolerance and adding robust wait helpers); e2e perf canary: pass on canary pool with 5-12% p99 latency improvement for mixed workloads; security scan: pass.
performance_summary: Canary results (canary pool, mixed interactive+long sequences): p50 unchanged, p95 improved by ~8%, p99 improved by ~12% for interactive (small-token) requests; tail latency for long sequence workload stable (+1-2%); overall throughput unchanged. Observed reduction in starvation events (defined as >200ms queue wait for short requests) by ~88%. Resource impact: negligible additional CPU; no GPU memory changes.
release_notes: Improved continuous batcher scheduler to reduce starvation and tail latency for mixed workloads. Add age-based priority, weighted admission for small requests, configurable preemption window, and per-request queue timeouts with graceful fallbacks. New metrics added to monitor queue wait and preemption events.
